newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal earns $135 million from Totta selloff.
newsitem.headline: Portugal earns $135 million from Totta selloff.

text.p: Portugal's government earned 20.5 billion escudos ($135 million) from the privatisation of a 13.22 percent stake in Portuguese bank Banco Totta e Acores (BTA) on Tuesday, officials said.
"I am pleased with the results," BTA president Alipio Dias told reporters at Lisbon bourse. "I think the price (2,630 escudos) reassures investors."

The sale at a fixed price of 2,630 escudos per share included a public offer to sell for 1.84 million shares, which was more than six times oversubscribed, and a domestic and international direct sale, officials said.
Dias said 800,000 shares were placed in the domestic direct sale and 5,289,471 shares in the international direct sale.
BTA employees acquired 635,000 shares and small investors and emigrants a total of 705,000 shares at a 10 percent discount from the fixed price.
The new shares will be listed on Lisbon bourse on Wednesday.

BTA shares rose on Lisbon bourse as some investors who could not fill their orders in the privatisation bought the stock, dealers said. BTA shares stood at 2,720 escudos, up 15, in volume of 52,431 shares in early afternoon trade.
